solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Social worker crosses very large slope

indicators.note: the worker bee straddles or spans the next piece, so it ends up wrapped round it

parts.note: a bee is the classic social insect that works in the hive
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A social worker is going over a very large slope, perhaps on a hillside visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a council employee but a BEE; 'crosses' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevel is a sloping edge cut on wood or glass, so it is a kind of slope.

clue.text: A lot of US money resting on film juvenile collecting Oscar

indicators.note: in a down answer this piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a buck is a US dollar
ET is the Spielberg film

indicators.note: the youngster gathers the next letter inside him

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Plenty of dollars are being made on a film about a youngster who picks up an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but is simply the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucketload is an informal quantity meaning a great deal.

clue.text: The sixth article's going through

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The sixth clause of a contract is being processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Via means by way of, passing through a place on a route.

clue.text: Polish way to draw in circles

indicators.note: in circles means the word for draw goes round the way, enclosing it

parts.note: to lure is to entice or draw
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A Polish method of drawing round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to mean from Poland; it is polish, shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the sheen a surface has, the shine that polish gives.

clue.text: Lover once noisily kissed soldier perhaps in the club

parts.note: a former partner is an ex

indicators.note: this tells us to say a word out loud and write down letters that sound like it

parts.note: to give a quick kiss is to peck, so kissed is pecked
a soldier ant is one kind of ant, so an ant is an example

explanation.surface: An old flame kissed a soldier loudly, apparently in some nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant, not a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectant describes a woman expecting a baby; 'in the club' is a British idiom meaning pregnant.

clue.text: Odd volume next to English books in Morecambe?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise; the question mark flags the example
CC, cubic centimetres, is a unit of volume
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An odd tome sits beside English books in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it stands for Eric Morecambe, a British TV comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric describes unconventional, peculiar behaviour, a synonym of odd.

clue.text: Healthy food that's often taken by nurses

definitions.meaning: lentils, beans and peas, a wholesome food

explanation.surface: A wholesome food that nurses are always eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is both an edible legume seed and the heartbeat rate measured at the wrist.

clue.text: Whitehall edifice not cheap to refurbish

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes the letters of not cheap in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Whitehall building will not be cheap to do up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to refurbish' rearranges NOTCHEAP. Whitehall is the London street of government offices where the national war memorial stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cenotaph is the war memorial standing in Whitehall, London.

clue.text: A firm imports chopped vegetable with increasing speed

indicators.note: the firm brings the following pieces inside itself

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: chopped means the vegetable loses its end letter

parts.note: celery is a vegetable
and means together with

explanation.surface: A company brings in cut-up vegetables with growing haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here but supplies AND; the definition is just 'increasing speed', a musical tempo direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Accelerando is the musical direction meaning gradually getting faster.

clue.text: Having put up fitting, chuck it down

indicators.note: in a down answer put up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper

explanation.surface: After putting up a light fitting, someone throws it to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chuck it down' looks like throwing something; it is British slang for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to pour with rain, which is what 'chuck it down' means informally.

clue.text: Traditional conservative girl I ring endlessly

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for ring is dropped

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A traditional Tory girl announces she rings people without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical style keeps to long-established, conventional forms, so it is traditional.

clue.text: New piece of ground that's acquired for buttons

parts.note: an acre is a measured area of land

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a new plot of land for next to nothing, 'for buttons'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For buttons' looks like 'very cheaply', but it means the material is wanted to make buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, mother-of-pearl, is the shell lining traditionally gathered to make pearly buttons.

clue.text: Briefly covet short story about strong guys in green

indicators.note: about means the trimmed pieces go around the strong men
cut short, so the last letter of the word for covet goes

parts.note: to covet is to envy

indicators.note: short means the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
iron men are tough, strong men

explanation.surface: Someone briefly envies a short story about muscular men in a green setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Briefly' and 'short' trim a last letter; 'about' has the two trimmed words surround the strong men, one on each side. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in politics means concerned for the natural world, which is what environmental means.

clue.text: One in six stops making appearances

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the stops

parts.note: stations are stops on a line
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One in six of the train stops is making an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitations are supernatural appearances, as of a ghost or divine being.

clue.text: Fellow bishop breaks deadlock

indicators.note: the bishop breaks into the deadlock, sitting inside it

parts.note: a stalemate is a deadlock, from chess
B is bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A chess bishop breaks a deadlocked game for a fellow player.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a companion from the same stable or organisation, a fellow.

clue.text: Flog city's hotel

parts.note: LA (Los Angeles) is the city, and with the 's it gives LA'S
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A short instruction to sell off the city's hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell, which suits the hotel, but here it means whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash someone is to beat them with a whip, which is to flog them.

clue.text: Nonconformist publican's gift?

definitions.meaning: a pub landlord handing over a ... means giving a whisky or gin on the house

explanation.surface: A rebel who is also the landlord's present to a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit is an independent, unconventional person; spirit is also a strong alcoholic drink, served free.

clue.text: Eg rubber dinghy catches cat after end of race

indicators.note: after places the dinghy piece behind the letter from race
end of means take the last letter of race
the dinghy captures the cat, holding it inside

parts.note: a Laser is a popular class of sailing dinghy
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A rubber dinghy picks up a cat after the race finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' seems to describe the dinghy, but 'Eg rubber' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastomer is any rubber-like elastic polymer; natural rubber is one example.

clue.text: Orcadian maybe is left with her, heading off

parts.note: and means with

indicators.note: heading off means remove the first letter of her

explanation.surface: A man from Orkney is left behind with his partner, who sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orcadian is someone from Orkney, the Scottish islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orcadian lives on Orkney's islands, so is an example of an islander.

clue.text: Spies among Latinos oddly withdrawn

indicators.note: among puts the spies inside the jumbled letters
oddly signals that the letters of Latinos are rearranged in a strange order

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Agents working among Latin Americans behave strangely and keep to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' jumbles the Latinos into ANTISOL, which the spies then sit 'among'; 'withdrawn' is the definition, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antisocial can mean unsociable, preferring one's own company, which is being withdrawn.

clue.text: Slight advance traps knight

indicators.note: the advance is wrapped round the knight, holding it inside

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money on wages
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A modest move forward catches a knight on the chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective but is the noun or verb meaning insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub is a deliberate insult, and to slight someone is to snub them.

clue.text: See regulation about importing old plush stuff

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: the turned word brings the next letter inside it
about means the word for regulation is turned round

parts.note: a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: A notice says see the rule on bringing in old luxury goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RULE into ELUR, and 'importing' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Velour is a plush fabric with a velvety pile.

clue.text: Battered bangers turn over hoarding where flag is

parts.note: TO is short for turn over, as in PTO at the foot of a page
a hoarding is a billboard carrying an ad
on a golf green the flag stands in the hole

explanation.surface: Damaged old cars turn over a billboard where a flag is flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers are British slang for both old cars and sausages; TOAD-IN-THE-HOLE is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is sausages cooked in batter, so it is literally sausages in batter.

clue.text: Restless in Berlin, I start to yawn, nursing temperature

indicators.note: the German word holds the next letter as if cradling it

parts.note: ich is German for I

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of yawn

explanation.surface: In Berlin I'm restless, yawning while nursing a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy can mean impatient or restless, as in itchy feet.

clue.text: Firm gets rid of one exchanged for cash

indicators.note: gets rid of means a letter is taken out of the word for firm

parts.note: solid means firm
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company sells off one item for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, which suits the sale, but it means solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold has been handed over in exchange for money.

clue.text: Elliptical old poet handling love

indicators.note: the poet holds the next piece in his hands, so it sits inside his name

parts.note: Ovid was a Roman poet of antiquity
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: An ancient poet deals with the subject of love in an elliptical way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elliptical' suggests obscure writing, fitting the poet, but means egg-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, an oval or ellipse-like solid shape.

clue.text: Current period ordinary citizen avoids initially

parts.note: a commoner is a citizen without noble rank

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of avoids

explanation.surface: These days an ordinary person tends to dodge things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current period' suggests electricity or a time span; it is the era we live in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the secular name for the dating system of the present age, CE.

clue.text: 24 eastern goods

parts.note: G is good, so two of them, GG, are goods

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a note about eastern goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is OVOID, meaning egg-shaped; the definition refers back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg is the model of an ovoid shape, so an ovoid object is like one.

clue.text: Warship restored after tangling with bow of yacht

indicators.note: the letters of restored, once tangled together with the next piece, are put in a new order
the bow is the front of a boat, so take the first letter of yacht

explanation.surface: A warship is restored after colliding with the bow of a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after tangling with' jumbles RESTORED plus Y; 'bow' cleverly keeps the nautical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast naval warship.

clue.text: Rake around good non-standard plant

indicators.note: the rake goes around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute man, a rake

explanation.surface: A gardener rakes around a good plant that is not the usual kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but is the old word for a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call a plant that differs from its variety's type a rogue, to be weeded out.
